findings.evidence: Description: "RL cells (human diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cell line)"; SDRF characteristics[disease]: "Burkitt lymphoma" in every row.
findings.explanation: The description says the RL cell line is a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma line. The SDRF records a different disease, Burkitt lymphoma, for all samples. This would give wrong disease annotation in downstream metadata and any repository submission.
findings.suggested_fix: Change characteristics[disease] to "diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" in all rows, unless the description is the one that is wrong.

findings.evidence: Rule check: "4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N." The description says: "Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: 12 samples use 12 of the 16 TMTpro channels, so four channels are empty. This matches the description, which says four channels are unused. The empty channels are the last four in the series (132C to 134N). The likely cause is that the experiment had only 12 samples. The unused channels will not affect the analysis. Empty channels should not be quantified, and they should not be treated as missing samples.
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed. Optionally note in the SDRF or the submission that TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C and TMT134N were intentionally left empty.

summary: One mismatch: the SDRF disease (Burkitt lymphoma) contradicts the description (diffuse large B-cell lymphoma). The four unused TMTpro channels are consistent with the description's 12 samples in a 16-plex kit.
